title: Geometric canary: can a cheap cosine statistic predict if a safety vector will work?

original_idea.body: For ~15 concepts compute cheap geometric statistics and test whether they predict real steering effectiveness, yielding a pre-flight don't-bother threshold.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful practical tool but mostly methodological/efficiency; chain to catastrophic-risk reduction is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Compute cheap cosine/separation stats + behavioral effect + rank correlation; standard tools, beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: 15 concepts, two statistics, predictive rank-correlation.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Training-free pre-flight tool, public data, no internal access; externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + cheap geometry on one model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Geometric reliability predictors are published; validating them as a cross-concept pre-flight check is partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Geometric predictors exist; validating them as a practical pre-flight check across many safety concepts may be open.
